title: New HIV vaccine shows unprecedented success in preclinical study
excerpt: Vaccine approach yields high numbers of HIV-neutralizing antibodies in non-human primates
content_html:
Highlights: 

  • Scientists at La Jolla Institute for Immunology, Scripps Research have developed an HIV vaccine that trains immune cells to see past HIV’s defenses.
  • This HIV vaccine works by prompting the body’s immune system to make substantial numbers of rarely seen “broadly neutralizing” antibodies.
  • In this new study, this vaccine resulted in the best HIV-fighting antibody response ever seen in primates. Human trials have now started.

LA JOLLA, CA—A new HIV vaccine developed by La Jolla Institute for Immunology (LJI), Scripps Research scientists, and IAVI has the potential to protect humans from developing HIV infection and AIDS. This HIV vaccine is the first to generate a high number of “broadly neutralizing,” virus-fighting antibodies in primates.

“This feels like a huge success,” says LJI Professor and Chief Scientific Officer Shane Crotty, Ph.D., who co-led the research with Scripps Research Professor William Schief, Ph.D. “We constructed a successful vaccine from the ground up, which required a deep understanding of the immune system.”

This groundbreaking research, published in Nature, is the result of 14 years of collaboration between La Jolla Institute for Immunology and Scripps Research, as part of the Scripps Consortium for HIV/AIDS Vaccine Development (CHAVD). “This has been one of those Apollo moon mission-type projects, where there is an exceptional goal and the team has to accomplish a myriad of discoveries and inventions along the way,” says Crotty.

Outsmarting HIV

The new vaccine works by intervening in a process called B cell maturation. B cells make antibodies. Like many immune cells, B cells have an early “naive” stage before they are ready to make antibodies. B cells start to mature once they get the signal that a pathogen, such as a virus, is trying to attack. B cells see pieces of that pathogen’s molecular structure and start producing antibodies that can bind to that structure and halt infection.

It can take a little while for B cells to find the right “bullseye” on a pathogen. But B cells keep trying. As they mature, B cells tweak their antibody production, refining antibody structures to bind to a pathogen in just the right, vulnerable spots.

Scientists describe B cell development as a training process or bootcamp. In most cases, the body is left with a well-honed B cell army.

HIV is hard to beat because it doesn’t give B cells a chance to develop effective antibodies. The first problem is that HIV disguises itself from the immune system. The virus is wrapped in an ever-shifting cloak of sugar molecules, called glycans. This lets HIV sneak undetected past human cells, which are also covered in glycans.

The second big problem is that HIV mutates very quickly. “The worldwide diversity of HIV mutations is extraordinary. Even the diversity within one individual person living with HIV is dramatic,” says LJI Instructor Patrick Madden, Ph.D., who served as study co-first author with Jon Steichen, Ph.D., an institute investigator at Scripps Research.

The third problem is that HIV changes its shape when it infects human cells. Even if B cells get a glimpse of its viral structure—snap!—the structure changes.

Taken together, these problems rarely give B cells a chance to hone their antibody responses against HIV. Even if a B cell manages to make neutralizing antibodies, the virus can mutate or change its shape, rendering those antibodies useless.

The LJI and Scripps Research teams spent years hunting for “broadly neutralizing” antibodies that can actually bind to HIV and recognize key viral structures, even if the rest of the virus mutates. These antibodies are very, very rare, but they can be found in blood samples from a small number of people living with HIV.

An effective HIV vaccine would need to prompt the immune system to make these same broadly neutralizing antibodies. “How could we flip the whole immune response on its head so the rare responses become the common responses? That was a critical challenge we faced,” says Crotty.

Testing the new vaccine

It was time to go back to B cell bootcamp. The scientists studied what made the HIV-fighting B cells special. Then they reversed the process to see exactly how those B cells matured. By looking back at the maturation process, the researchers could track how the B cells changed when they saw specific pieces of the HIV structure.

The team discovered that B cells matured to make broadly neutralizing antibodies after they got an early look at parts of HIV’s outer “envelope” protein. Because these viral sites sparked an immune response, scientists would call them “antigens.” 

An effective HIV vaccine would likely need to include models of these antigens. The antigens would work like mugshots of America’s most wanted. If B cells saw those antigens early and often, they would get really good at recognizing and even neutralizing HIV. “We were trying to mimic the progression of those neutralizing antibodies,” says Madden.

In a feat of molecular engineering, the Schief Lab developed vaccine molecules that resembled the real HIV antigens. The scientists then worked with Emory National Primate Research Center, to test this potential HIV vaccine in a non-human primate species called rhesus macaques.

The researchers first administered a “priming” vaccine meant to activate each animal’s naive B cells. The animals then received a series of “shepherding” booster shots to help their B cells develop along the right path. 

“This series of vaccinations will guide, or ‘walk’, a B cell from its naive state to its broadly neutralizing state,” says Madden.

This new type of vaccine approach is called “germline targeting” because it targets naive B cells in their “germline” or naive form, before they begin their training process.

The scientists found that around 44 percent of the animals went on to produce broadly neutralizing antibodies against HIV in their blood. These antibodies were impressively abundant. 

“We succeeded in taking ultra-rare antibody responses and turning them into common responses by the end of the vaccination process,” adds Crotty. In other research recently published, they reported a new strategy to accelerate related vaccine antibody responses [See Nature Immunology paper].

The team didn’t test whether these antibodies could prevent infection, but it’s significant that these antibodies could be found in the blood, where they could encounter and potentially block HIV.

Bringing the HIV vaccine to humans

The Crotty Lab plans to investigate how they might change the booster shot regimen to make the HIV vaccine even more effective. “It was incredible to get those results, but of course we’d like to see a response in 100 percent of the animals,” says Madden. 

Importantly, the antibodies found in the animal subjects resembled the exact kinds of broadly neutralizing antibodies seen in those rare humans who made their own neutralizing antibodies. It’s clear that our immune systems can make these powerful antibodies, given the right training.

“We believe this vaccine approach is even more likely to succeed in humans, because of the immunogenetics,” Crotty says.

The priming immunogen used in this study was evaluated in humans in the HVTN 144 trial and is currently being tested in the Phase 1 trial IAVI G004. IAVI, Scripps Research, the HIV Vaccine Trials Network, and partners are now advancing plans to further evaluate the full immunization regimen in a future human clinical study.

sentences.en: The LJI and Scripps Research teams spent years hunting for “broadly neutralizing” antibodies that can actually bind to HIV and recognize key viral structures, even if the rest of the virus mutates.
sentences.zh: LJI 和斯克里普斯研究团队花了数年时间寻找“广泛中和”抗体，这些抗体实际上可以与 HIV 结合并识别关键的病毒结构，即使病毒的其余部分发生了突变。

sentences.en: These antibodies are very, very rare, but they can be found in blood samples from a small number of people living with HIV.
sentences.zh: 这些抗体非常非常罕见，但可以在少数艾滋病毒感染者的血液样本中找到。

blocks.html_en: An effective HIV vaccine would need to prompt the immune system to make these same broadly neutralizing antibodies. “How could we flip the whole immune response on its head so the rare responses become the common responses? That was a critical challenge we faced,” says Crotty.

sentences.en: An effective HIV vaccine would need to prompt the immune system to make these same broadly neutralizing antibodies.
sentences.zh: 有效的艾滋病毒疫苗需要促使免疫系统产生这些相同的广泛中和抗体。

sentences.en: “How could we flip the whole immune response on its head so the rare responses become the common responses?
sentences.zh: “我们怎样才能彻底改变整个免疫反应，使罕见的反应变成常见的反应？

sentences.en: That was a critical challenge we faced,” says Crotty.
sentences.zh: 这是我们面临的一个严峻挑战，”克罗蒂说。

blocks.html_en: Testing the new vaccine

sentences.en: Testing the new vaccine
sentences.zh: 测试新疫苗

blocks.html_en: It was time to go back to B cell bootcamp. The scientists studied what made the HIV-fighting B cells special. Then they reversed the process to see exactly how those B cells matured. By looking back at the maturation process, the researchers could track how the B cells changed when they saw specific pieces of the HIV structure.

sentences.en: It was time to go back to B cell bootcamp.
sentences.zh: 是时候回到 B 细胞训练营了。

sentences.en: The scientists studied what made the HIV-fighting B cells special.
sentences.zh: 科学家们研究了抗 HIV B 细胞的特殊之处。

sentences.en: Then they reversed the process to see exactly how those B cells matured.
sentences.zh: 然后他们逆转了这个过程，以准确观察这些 B 细胞是如何成熟的。

sentences.en: By looking back at the maturation process, the researchers could track how the B cells changed when they saw specific pieces of the HIV structure.
sentences.zh: 通过回顾成熟过程，研究人员可以追踪 B 细胞在看到 HIV 结构的特定片段时如何变化。

blocks.html_en: The team discovered that B cells matured to make broadly neutralizing antibodies after they got an early look at parts of HIV’s outer “envelope” protein. Because these viral sites sparked an immune response, scientists would call them “antigens.”

sentences.en: The team discovered that B cells matured to make broadly neutralizing antibodies after they got an early look at parts of HIV’s outer “envelope” protein.
sentences.zh: 研究小组发现，在早期观察到 HIV 外层“包膜”蛋白的部分内容后，B 细胞成熟后能够产生广泛的中和抗体。

sentences.en: Because these viral sites sparked an immune response, scientists would call them “antigens.”
sentences.zh: 由于这些病毒位点引发了免疫反应，科学家将它们称为“抗原”。

blocks.html_en: An effective HIV vaccine would likely need to include models of these antigens. The antigens would work like mugshots of America’s most wanted. If B cells saw those antigens early and often, they would get really good at recognizing and even neutralizing HIV. “We were trying to mimic the progression of those neutralizing antibodies,” says Madden.

sentences.en: An effective HIV vaccine would likely need to include models of these antigens.
sentences.zh: 有效的艾滋病毒疫苗可能需要包括这些抗原的模型。

sentences.en: The antigens would work like mugshots of America’s most wanted.
sentences.zh: 这些抗原的作用就像美国头号通缉犯的照片一样。

sentences.en: If B cells saw those antigens early and often, they would get really good at recognizing and even neutralizing HIV.
sentences.zh: 如果 B 细胞尽早且经常发现这些抗原，它们就会非常擅长识别甚至中和 HIV。

sentences.en: “We were trying to mimic the progression of those neutralizing antibodies,” says Madden.
sentences.zh: “我们试图模仿这些中和抗体的进展，”马登说。

blocks.html_en: In a feat of molecular engineering, the Schief Lab developed vaccine molecules that resembled the real HIV antigens. The scientists then worked with Emory National Primate Research Center, to test this potential HIV vaccine in a non-human primate species called rhesus macaques.

sentences.en: In a feat of molecular engineering, the Schief Lab developed vaccine molecules that resembled the real HIV antigens.
sentences.zh: 在分子工程的一项壮举中，希夫实验室开发了类似于真正的艾滋病毒抗原的疫苗分子。

sentences.en: The scientists then worked with Emory National Primate Research Center, to test this potential HIV vaccine in a non-human primate species called rhesus macaques.
sentences.zh: 随后，科学家们与埃默里国家灵长类动物研究中心合作，在一种称为恒河猴的非人类灵长类动物身上测试了这种潜在的艾滋病毒疫苗。

blocks.html_en: The researchers first administered a “priming” vaccine meant to activate each animal’s naive B cells. The animals then received a series of “shepherding” booster shots to help their B cells develop along the right path.

sentences.en: The researchers first administered a “priming” vaccine meant to activate each animal’s naive B cells.
sentences.zh: 研究人员首先注射了一种“启动”疫苗，旨在激活每只动物的初始 B 细胞。

sentences.en: The animals then received a series of “shepherding” booster shots to help their B cells develop along the right path.
sentences.zh: 然后，这些动物接受了一系列“引导”加强注射，以帮助它们的 B 细胞沿着正确的道路发育。

blocks.html_en: “This series of vaccinations will guide, or ‘walk’, a B cell from its naive state to its broadly neutralizing state,” says Madden.

sentences.en: “This series of vaccinations will guide, or ‘walk’, a B cell from its naive state to its broadly neutralizing state,” says Madden.
sentences.zh: Madden 说：“这一系列疫苗将引导或‘行走’B 细胞从初始状态进入广泛的中和状态。”

blocks.html_en: This new type of vaccine approach is called “germline targeting” because it targets naive B cells in their “germline” or naive form, before they begin their training process.

sentences.en: This new type of vaccine approach is called “germline targeting” because it targets naive B cells in their “germline” or naive form, before they begin their training process.
sentences.zh: 这种新型疫苗方法被称为“种系靶向”，因为它在幼稚 B 细胞开始训练过程之前以“种系”或幼稚形式为目标。

blocks.html_en: The scientists found that around 44 percent of the animals went on to produce broadly neutralizing antibodies against HIV in their blood. These antibodies were impressively abundant.

sentences.en: The scientists found that around 44 percent of the animals went on to produce broadly neutralizing antibodies against HIV in their blood.
sentences.zh: 科学家发现，大约 44% 的动物在血液中产生了针对 HIV 的广泛中和抗体。

sentences.en: These antibodies were impressively abundant.
sentences.zh: 这些抗体的丰富程度令人印象深刻。

blocks.html_en: “We succeeded in taking ultra-rare antibody responses and turning them into common responses by the end of the vaccination process,” adds Crotty. In other research recently published, they reported a new strategy to accelerate related vaccine antibody responses [See Nature Immunology paper].

sentences.en: “We succeeded in taking ultra-rare antibody responses and turning them into common responses by the end of the vaccination process,” adds Crotty.
sentences.zh: “我们成功地获得了极其罕见的抗体反应，并在疫苗接种过程结束时将它们转化为常见的反应，”克罗蒂补充道。

sentences.en: In other research recently published, they reported a new strategy to accelerate related vaccine antibody responses [See Nature Immunology paper].
sentences.zh: 在最近发表的其他研究中，他们报告了一种加速相关疫苗抗体反应的新策略[参见《自然免疫学》论文]。

blocks.html_en: The team didn’t test whether these antibodies could prevent infection, but it’s significant that these antibodies could be found in the blood, where they could encounter and potentially block HIV.

sentences.en: The team didn’t test whether these antibodies could prevent infection, but it’s significant that these antibodies could be found in the blood, where they could encounter and potentially block HIV.
sentences.zh: 研究小组没有测试这些抗体是否可以预防感染，但重要的是，这些抗体可以在血液中找到，它们可以在血液中遇到并可能阻止艾滋病毒。

blocks.html_en: Bringing the HIV vaccine to humans

sentences.en: Bringing the HIV vaccine to humans
sentences.zh: 将艾滋病毒疫苗带给人类

blocks.html_en: The Crotty Lab plans to investigate how they might change the booster shot regimen to make the HIV vaccine even more effective. “It was incredible to get those results, but of course we’d like to see a response in 100 percent of the animals,” says Madden.

sentences.en: The Crotty Lab plans to investigate how they might change the booster shot regimen to make the HIV vaccine even more effective.
sentences.zh: Crotty 实验室计划研究如何改变加强注射方案，以使艾滋病毒疫苗更加有效。

sentences.en: “It was incredible to get those results, but of course we’d like to see a response in 100 percent of the animals,” says Madden.
sentences.zh: “获得这些结果令人难以置信，但我们当然希望看到 100% 的动物都有反应，”Madden 说。

blocks.html_en: Importantly, the antibodies found in the animal subjects resembled the exact kinds of broadly neutralizing antibodies seen in those rare humans who made their own neutralizing antibodies. It’s clear that our immune systems can make these powerful antibodies, given the right training.

sentences.en: Importantly, the antibodies found in the animal subjects resembled the exact kinds of broadly neutralizing antibodies seen in those rare humans who made their own neutralizing antibodies.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，在动物受试者中发现的抗体与在那些自己产生中和抗体的罕见人类中看到的广泛中和抗体的种类完全相同。

sentences.en: It’s clear that our immune systems can make these powerful antibodies, given the right training.
sentences.zh: 很明显，只要经过正确的训练，我们的免疫系统就可以产生这些强大的抗体。

blocks.html_en: “We believe this vaccine approach is even more likely to succeed in humans, because of the immunogenetics,” Crotty says.

sentences.en: “We believe this vaccine approach is even more likely to succeed in humans, because of the immunogenetics,” Crotty says.
sentences.zh: “我们相信，由于免疫遗传学的原因，这种疫苗方法更有可能在人类身上取得成功，”克罗蒂说。

blocks.html_en: The priming immunogen used in this study was evaluated in humans in the HVTN 144 trial and is currently being tested in the Phase 1 trial IAVI G004. IAVI, Scripps Research, the HIV Vaccine Trials Network, and partners are now advancing plans to further evaluate the full immunization regimen in a future human clinical study.

content_html_zh:
亮点：

  • 斯克里普斯研究所拉霍亚免疫学研究所的科学家们开发出了一种艾滋病毒疫苗，可以训练免疫细胞突破艾滋病毒的防御。
  • 这种艾滋病毒疫苗的作用是促使人体的免疫系统产生大量罕见的“广泛中和”抗体。
  • 在这项新研究中，这种疫苗在灵长类动物中产生了有史以来最好的抗艾滋病毒抗体反应。 人体试验现已开始。

加利福尼亚州拉霍拉——拉霍亚免疫学研究所 (LJI)、斯克里普斯研究中心的科学家和 IAVI 开发的一种新型 HIV 疫苗有可能保护人类免遭 HIV 感染和艾滋病。 这种艾滋病毒疫苗是第一个在灵长类动物体内产生大量“广泛中和”病毒的抗体的疫苗。

“这感觉像是一个巨大的成功，”LJI 教授兼首席科学官 Shane Crotty 博士说道，他与斯克里普斯研究教授 William Schief 博士共同领导了这项研究。 “我们从头开始构建了一种成功的疫苗，这需要对免疫系统有深入的了解。”

这项发表在《自然》杂志上的突破性研究是拉霍亚免疫学研究所和斯克里普斯研究所 14 年合作的成果，斯克里普斯研究所是斯克里普斯艾滋病毒/艾滋病疫苗开发联盟 (CHAVD) 的一部分。 “这是阿波罗登月任务类型的项目之一，有一个特殊的目标，团队必须一路完成无数的发现和发明，”克罗蒂说。

智胜艾滋病毒

新疫苗通过干预 B 细胞成熟过程发挥作用。 B 细胞产生抗体。 与许多免疫细胞一样，B 细胞在准备好产生抗体之前有一个早期的“幼稚”阶段。 一旦 B 细胞收到病原体（例如病毒）试图攻击的信号，它们就会开始成熟。 B 细胞看到该病原体的分子结构片段，并开始产生可以与该结构结合并阻止感染的抗体。

B 细胞可能需要一段时间才能找到病原体的正确“靶心”。 但 B 细胞仍在不断尝试。 当 B 细胞成熟时，它们会调整抗体的产生，完善抗体结构，以便在适当的、脆弱的位置与病原体结合。

科学家将 B 细胞发育描述为训练过程或训练营。 在大多数情况下，身体会留下一支经过精心训练的 B 细胞军队。

HIV 很难被击败，因为它无法让 B 细胞有机会产生有效的抗体。 第一个问题是艾滋病毒会伪装自己以躲避免疫系统。 该病毒被包裹在不断变化的糖分子（称为聚糖）中。 这使得艾滋病毒能够在未被发现的情况下潜入人体细胞，而人体细胞也被聚糖覆盖。

第二个大问题是艾滋病病毒变异非常快。 “全球艾滋病毒突变的多样性是非同寻常的。 即使是一个艾滋病毒感染者个体的多样性也是巨大的，”LJI 讲师 Patrick Madden 博士说道，他与 Scripps Research 研究所研究员 Jon Steichen 博士共同担任该研究的共同第一作者。

第三个问题是，艾滋病病毒感染人体细胞后会改变形状。 即使 B 细胞瞥见了病毒的结构——啪！——结构也会发生变化。

总而言之，这些问题很少让 B 细胞有机会磨练针对 HIV 的抗体反应。 即使 B 细胞设法产生中和抗体，病毒也可能发生突变或改变其形状，使这些抗体变得无用。

LJI 和斯克里普斯研究团队花了数年时间寻找“广泛中和”抗体，这些抗体实际上可以与 HIV 结合并识别关键的病毒结构，即使病毒的其余部分发生了突变。 这些抗体非常非常罕见，但可以在少数艾滋病毒感染者的血液样本中找到。

有效的艾滋病毒疫苗需要促使免疫系统产生这些相同的广泛中和抗体。 “我们怎样才能彻底改变整个免疫反应，使罕见的反应变成常见的反应？ 这是我们面临的一个严峻挑战，”克罗蒂说。

测试新疫苗

是时候回到 B 细胞训练营了。 科学家们研究了抗 HIV B 细胞的特殊之处。 然后他们逆转了这个过程，以准确观察这些 B 细胞是如何成熟的。 通过回顾成熟过程，研究人员可以追踪 B 细胞在看到 HIV 结构的特定片段时如何变化。

研究小组发现，在早期观察到 HIV 外层“包膜”蛋白的部分内容后，B 细胞成熟后能够产生广泛的中和抗体。 由于这些病毒位点引发了免疫反应，科学家将它们称为“抗原”。

有效的艾滋病毒疫苗可能需要包括这些抗原的模型。 这些抗原的作用就像美国头号通缉犯的照片一样。 如果 B 细胞尽早且经常发现这些抗原，它们就会非常擅长识别甚至中和 HIV。 “我们试图模仿这些中和抗体的进展，”马登说。

在分子工程的一项壮举中，希夫实验室开发了类似于真正的艾滋病毒抗原的疫苗分子。 随后，科学家们与埃默里国家灵长类动物研究中心合作，在一种称为恒河猴的非人类灵长类动物身上测试了这种潜在的艾滋病毒疫苗。

研究人员首先注射了一种“启动”疫苗，旨在激活每只动物的初始 B 细胞。 然后，这些动物接受了一系列“引导”加强注射，以帮助它们的 B 细胞沿着正确的道路发育。

Madden 说：“这一系列疫苗将引导或‘行走’B 细胞从初始状态进入广泛的中和状态。”

这种新型疫苗方法被称为“种系靶向”，因为它在幼稚 B 细胞开始训练过程之前以“种系”或幼稚形式为目标。

科学家发现，大约 44% 的动物在血液中产生了针对 HIV 的广泛中和抗体。 这些抗体的丰富程度令人印象深刻。

“我们成功地获得了极其罕见的抗体反应，并在疫苗接种过程结束时将它们转化为常见的反应，”克罗蒂补充道。 在最近发表的其他研究中，他们报告了一种加速相关疫苗抗体反应的新策略[参见《自然免疫学》论文]。

研究小组没有测试这些抗体是否可以预防感染，但重要的是，这些抗体可以在血液中找到，它们可以在血液中遇到并可能阻止艾滋病毒。

将艾滋病毒疫苗带给人类

Crotty 实验室计划研究如何改变加强注射方案，以使艾滋病毒疫苗更加有效。 “获得这些结果令人难以置信，但我们当然希望看到 100% 的动物都有反应，”Madden 说。

重要的是，在动物受试者中发现的抗体与在那些自己产生中和抗体的罕见人类中看到的广泛中和抗体的种类完全相同。 很明显，只要经过正确的训练，我们的免疫系统就可以产生这些强大的抗体。

“我们相信，由于免疫遗传学的原因，这种疫苗方法更有可能在人类身上取得成功，”克罗蒂说。

本研究中使用的引发免疫原在 HVTN 144 试验中对人体进行了评估，目前正在 1 期试验 IAVI G004 中进行测试。 IAVI、斯克里普斯研究中心、艾滋病毒疫苗试验网络和合作伙伴目前正在推进计划，以在未来的人类临床研究中进一步评估完整的免疫方案。
